subject.title: Feature: Handle Signal message edits (editMessage envelope)

question: Should Signal edits dispatch as marked corrections, supersede the original transcript entry, or update context without a new turn unless mention policy matches?
rationale: The upstream envelope establishes that an edit occurred, but existing OpenClaw behavior does not define which session-state and response semantic should be canonical.

options.title: Dispatch Marked Correction
options.body: Carry structured edit metadata and target identity through normal inbound dispatch while preserving the original event history.

options.title: Supersede Original Context
options.body: Replace or invalidate the original transcript entry through a generic, persistence-safe session-edit contract.

options.title: Mention-Gated Silent Update
options.body: Record corrected content but start a new group turn only when the edited text satisfies mention policy.

recommendation.title: Dispatch Marked Correction
recommendation.body: Carry structured edit metadata and target identity through normal inbound dispatch while preserving the original event history.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history signal is the original and foundational Signal inbound implementation work.
